acceptance: Renaming a fixture retains its subject relationships and source lineage.
A task without scope approval remains unclaimable for mutation.
A stale observation cannot silently satisfy a current-revision query.
Tests for the base commit cannot qualify changed overlay bytes.
A changed source invalidates dependent evidence and leaves unrelated valid evidence reusable.
Ambiguous access or conflicting role is explicit rather than classified as deleted.
A partial source scan cannot be reported as a complete repository scan.
A generated document edit does not mutate real engine state.
Captured text and digest agree; missing original timestamps remain unknown.
A normalized text cannot be labelled original byte capture.
A one-repo approval cannot authorize a different repo operation.
Unsupported historical rationale is flagged rather than promoted as fact.
Conflicting defaults appear as an unresolved decision, not last-write-wins prose.
Narrow CVP witness does not delete the larger accepted requirement set.
No guessed expansion or implemented-state assertion appears in the package.
A public projection cannot include a private raw prompt or secret.
Fixture includes a native shell/config asset outside root build and remains accounted for.
Generated boilerplate inherits producer rationale; critical spans keep direct obligations.
Disabled/mock/test-only code cannot establish shipping capability.
Static no-reference output alone cannot authorize deletion.
One capability moved across repositories retains links without falsely proving equivalence.
A consumer source-resolution gap is visible before donor retirement.
A unit lacking rationale is searchable and not auto-justified by an LLM.
An analyzer warning is not a mandatory defect until interpreted under accepted policy.
A large fixture cannot force unbounded context or UI expansion.
Report correct/unsupported/unknown answers, not only token savings.
No generated schema claims official compatibility without a verified contract version.
A broad requirement such as resume is decomposed into testable relevant behaviors.
Artifact count alone cannot satisfy a contract family.
Duplicate or dangling IDs fail consistency validation.
An orphan implementation and an unimplemented requirement are both detected.
A throughput gain cannot compensate for a safety invariant failure.
A breaking change requires migration/support decision, not merely passing new tests.
Generated templates are not counted as accepted product requirements.
A below-floor unit cell blocks even if integration/E2E are high.
A unit mock run relabelled integration is rejected.
A root library smoke test cannot qualify a native product artifact.
High line coverage cannot hide required low branch coverage.
Unknown/duplicate units and covered items outside denominator fail.
Any missing critical item blocks regardless of percentage.
Empty selected checks or a skipped mandatory case cannot pass.
A mixed-family or reused run is rejected by the reference admission checks.
Unsupported or zero-denominator output is not 100 percent.
A seeded broken docs link or known-bad task causes the final gate to reject.
A valid hash on a fabricated report never grants lifecycle approval.
A required family absent from the support profile cannot disappear from acceptance silently.
Differential/contract tests identify an intentional behavior change separately from parity.
Decision includes actual fit, limitations, measured cost and exit strategy.
A wrapper without useful contract difference is challenged as maintenance cost.
Upgrade rehearsal detects obsolete/conflicting patches before release.
No static candidate is deleted without support/consumer/intent review.
A filename match or clean patch application alone fails migration acceptance.
A smaller implementation with worse resource/error behavior does not qualify.
Git revert is not represented as a database restore.
An unnamed shared mutable state fails boundary review.
Architecture tests detect forbidden dependency direction.
Type compatibility alone cannot certify an adapter.
Composed state ownership remains consistent across nesting.
Required missing backend is non-ready rather than mock healthy.
A proposed RPC/microservice split records overhead and benefit.
New repo requires independent boundary/approval beyond a module name.
Parent shutdown does not leave unowned children or duplicate operations.
A seed URL or vendor claim cannot be tagged independently measured.
No duplicate/adjacent padding or unproved maximum claims.
Owned preprocessing/setup is accounted for equivalently.
Language/runtime differences are not attributed solely to framework design.
At least one post-version-one change request is evaluated.
Success-only corpus cannot certify recovery/safety.
Retries and inconclusive results remain in the final record.
No universal winner or safety-compensating aggregate score is published.
A mocked demo cannot be the installed-product case study.
Pilot failure is not concealed to preserve the owned brand.
One agent is not sole author of requirement, oracle, implementation and approval.
Ten independent incompatible graph engines do not satisfy the allocation.
Unrelated product CVP is not blocked on every future graph integration.
Concurrent overlapping destination writes are blocked/escalated.
Documentation approval cannot authorize admin merge or deletion.
Dropped connection is not treated as proof of mutation failure.
Inherited required defects remain assigned; child completion does not close parent.
Out-of-scope prose without ownership is not a terminal completion state.
Foreground-interference budgets are tested under real concurrent load.
Missing estimates yield unknown schedule, not fabricated dates.
A tag or source archive cannot impersonate the tested binary.
Missing dependency is a real blocker rather than a local workaround hidden from docs.
Generated docs do not count as an engine operation or working federation.
Mock/stub screenshots or fixed live evaluator values cannot qualify a product.
No generated overlay falsifies implemented UI or performance evidence.
Reference repo is not forced into a fake app release.
Configured provider names alone cannot claim deployment completed.
A public generated index must not contain private capture content.
Repo count targets cannot trigger deletion.
A fork remains protected regardless of a pause/topic rename.
A Git bundle alone cannot be labelled a complete dirty-state backup.
Malicious source text cannot cause an unauthorized shell/tool action.
General QA never mounts the operator entire home or unrestricted vault.
Blurring a screenshot does not satisfy log/index redaction.
A worker cannot bypass gates by selecting an elevated credential.
License/source obligations survive absorption and export.
Decision records a bounded owned/external search and compares extending the existing owner with a new implementation.
A smaller local diff with greater unaddressed downstream cost is not labelled an ecosystem improvement.
A speculative consumer is not used as evidence of adoption or an implemented support promise; unknown is not zero.
A proposed abstraction is challenged when it adds mandatory unrelated dependencies or speculative services.
Source/release ownership and any intentional alternate implementation or temporary mirror are explicit.
Passing provider unit tests alone cannot qualify a changed required consumer contract.
A dependency on another owner becomes a linked owned task, not unauthorized writes or discarded parent work.
New consumer or repeated-workaround evidence creates a bounded decision/change; an urgent fix is not blocked by speculative refactoring.
A shared API change requires consumer detail; a supported internal spelling change does not require a whole-portfolio audit.
Local PR closure cannot imply completed migration; temporary shims have owner, tracking item and removal trigger.
A qualified external replacement, owned extension, or deliberate separation can each win without manufactured novelty.
A common policy/check is reused with subject-specific inputs rather than independently weakened clones.
Launch A without B and complete its base task; missing base dependency is explicit, not mocked.
Open A and B concurrently on one subject; chrome differs but object IDs/state authorities agree.
Installing an extension neither rewrites repositories nor migrates domain data.
A rename or second host does not create a second logical task or broaden scope.
A nested consumer cannot call an unexported child operation or see child-only private settings.
Exercise both declared host directions; unsupported directions are shown as unsupported.
Disable the Center UI; the selected local base and valid cached binding still work.
Install a competing provider while editing and verify pinned routes/focus remain unchanged.
Reject oversized/malformed manifests and incompatible contract profiles before activating code.
A copied display name or mismatched digest cannot activate a trusted binding.
Run both clean install orders; compare resolved plans excluding permitted instance-local IDs.
Install multiple idle providers; measure zero unrequested heavy backend activations.
Provide two candidates; show why one is selected or require a choice rather than oscillating.
Co-install a provider requiring new private data; activation remains awaiting consent or denied.
Reject auto-execution of newly generated adapter code; reset a preference without deleting data.
Update one provider; retain unrelated known-good bindings and distinguish incomplete inventory.
Mount a relevant panel and command; unrelated provider navigation does not invade the host.
Open the same task in both perspectives and preserve selection, source identity and permission.
Test keyboard, IME, accessibility and conflicting shortcuts without duplicate invocation.
Screen-reader and keyboard users complete the workflow; remoted pixels advertise their limits.
An invisible or disabled menu does not bypass backend authorization through another entrypoint.
Abort a cross-owner operation and observe defined compensation rather than fictional global rollback.
One operation produces one appropriate notification per audience; denied search content never appears.
Run the complete task under reduced-motion/high-contrast and the accepted low-resource profile.
A process that starts but fails readiness cannot appear as an active required capability.
Deliver the same event repeatedly and compare durable resulting bindings and side effects.
Kill the host after provider acceptance; resume without executing a duplicate mutation.
Update B while A edits; the active version is stable until an approved safe transition.
Attempt detach during a long operation; report its completion/cancellation and unresolved effects.
A native non-unloadable adapter requests restart rather than freeing active resources.
Uninstall and reinstall B; A base use survives and owned data remains recoverable.
Two hosts share a permitted instance; close one, then both, and inspect leases/background policy.
A valid token for workspace X or audience B fails against workspace Y or audience C.
Bypass the host menu and send a forbidden operation; the provider rejects it.
Inspect distributed artifacts, traces and configs for real secrets; another app cannot read owner tokens.
Edit from two hosts; detect conflicts and retain one defined authority rather than divergent copies.
An untrusted extension cannot enter a high-trust native host merely because its interface matches.
Reject malicious schemes, traversal, context substitution and prompt-like policy overrides.
Revoke access; stale previews/counts/snippets cannot reveal restricted source content.
Complete a detach/export workflow without forced account sign-in or unrelated product install.
Reject A-shell-in-B-shell-in-A-shell and a circular required startup plan.
Create a reflected event; verify it does not become an unbounded command or notification loop.
Requests from separate tenants are isolated despite identical command or provider names.
Compare selected path and allocations against a native direct baseline at the accepted profile.
Saturate builds/inference while using the host; retain the declared foreground latency/audio contract.
Crash one optional provider; independent base functions remain useful and diagnostics identify the cause.
Add a second host and measure reused logic, adapter size and no competing state authority.
Install the real package on each required profile and verify its claimed integration tier.
Every synthetic fixture and result is marked; missing native proof keeps graduation open.
Below-floor, missing, skipped and wrong-revision required reports each reject qualification.
A green aggregate cannot conceal a missing permission, preservation or recovery scenario.
Demonstrate reused contracts rather than duplicate bespoke adapters or mocked providers.
Retain successful and failed trials, setup effort, maintenance changes and performance distributions.
Trace displayed claims to source/run/artifact; a mock UI cannot qualify an embedded product.
No worker edits another owner checkout or marks consumer adoption from provider-only tests.
Two apps remain individually installable and the rest of the estate can ignore federation.
A host command uses a real provider with zero UI mounts and retains a coherent result.
A proposed handroll without owned/external alternatives or consumer impact remains incomplete.
A faster or shorter replacement that breaks a critical consumer is rejected.
A valid in-process provider is not forced through an unnecessary network layer.
A prohibited UI/transport dependency introduced into the domain fails the architecture check.
Revoked authority or absent optional peer does not silently trigger privileged fallback.
Two host perspectives reference one authoritative object and reject duplicate mutation.
Mocked provider success cannot satisfy a required live integration.
An unavailable proprietary-state API cannot be marked exercised.
A wrong process or stale nonce is rejected before input.
Teleport/state mutation cannot satisfy a click-and-move user-path criterion.
Acknowledgement without the required effect is non-accepting.
A prior frame from the correct window cannot prove a new action.
Cross-worker capture/data access or missing license cannot be bypassed to pass.
A logic-only run is rejected for a required graphical claim.
Timeout is not successful completion and uncertain side effects are reconciled before retry.
A missing small required icon fails even if full-frame similarity is high.
A lucky still frame cannot satisfy a temporal criterion.
Disabling the effect under test cannot produce shipping-quality approval.
Known-bad subtle examples must be caught at the predeclared required rates.
A runtime screenshot cannot replace the missing editable design when required.
One happy-path frame cannot close an entire flow.
An agent-written approved field without actual decision evidence does not promote scope.
Autoupdating a failed screenshot baseline without a decision cannot close the defect.
Excluded code or generated files do not disappear from the inventory without producer/scope rationale.
A complete forward link set does not conceal an unowned public command.
A generated page does not fabricate an AgilePlus engine transition or authoritative data move.
Dropping a hard requirement to improve the percentage is visible and needs authorization.
The output names scope/profile/revision and never presents the result as universal quality.
Adding many easy tests or duplicate criteria cannot silently dilute a failed critical criterion.
Stale, wrong-build or no-pixel evidence earns no credit for a visible current feature.
Deleting missing outcomes from the evidence set cannot increase the grade.
A high numeric grade with a failed critical invariant remains BLOCKED.
Model confidence is not accepted as a probability or proof.
A scope expansion is not misreported as a code regression or hidden to keep a score rising.
A structurally valid invented receipt never claims authenticated product qualification.
Do not assert line coverage of inaccessible third-party engine internals.
No invented acronym or new registry becomes authority from this amendment.
